newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch government against Laarbruch airport initiative.
newsitem.headline: Dutch government against Laarbruch airport initiative.

text.p: The Dutch government has decided not to back an initiative designed to transform Laarbruch, a British military base into an airfreight hub, said the Dutch Minister of Transport in a letter to the major of New Bergen, a town near the base.
New Bergen council had asked the Dutch government to make a statement on the proposed project.
Under the title "Airport Niederrhein", the German initiative, aims to develop the Royal Airforce base, which is due to close in 1999, as a civilian airfreight hub.

The Dutch government state that noise levels would be unacceptable. But as well as this, the Dutch argue that the development would bring a serious safety risk to jets deployed at a neighbouring airfield where the Dutch Royal Airforce has a base.
Risks would increase because civil aircraft need a longer flight path than the military jets so they would be brought close to the jets, said the Dutch government.
The project team is expected to get a clear answer from the German authorites as to whether the initiative can go-ahead in April 1997. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
